index.title: SFERA Lab — Free Natal Chart (Research Prototype)
index.description: A free Western natal chart computed in your browser by a deterministic engine (differentially verified against the lab's Python kernel — agreement, not proof of truth). Research prototype: no accounts, no tracking, nothing stored.
index.h1: Free natal chart — computed from ephemeris data, not generated by AI
index.intro: SFERA Lab is an experimental research environment for computational astrology, interpretation systems and AI-assisted comparative research. This page computes a Western (tropical) natal chart with a deterministic engine that is differentially verified against the lab's Python kernel (260 frozen cases, 0 failures — engine agreement, not proof of truth; methodology), with full disclosure of method, conventions and school labels. No AI text is generated here. The calculation runs entirely in your browser — your birth data never leaves your device. No accounts, no tracking, nothing stored. 18+ only. How it works, and what it is not.
index.measurement: Measurement, precisely stated: without your consent nothing is sent — not even the fact of a visit. If you tick the consent box, anonymous usage events (funnel stages, no birth data) may be sent to a minimal research sink. Exactly what is sent: the privacy explanation.
index.city_privacy: City search sends your typed query to Open-Meteo (GeoNames catalog). Date, time, question and chart data are never sent.
index.f_time_hint: — leave empty if unknown; the chart then suppresses (does not guess) the Moon degree, angles and houses
index.f_tz: Time zone (IANA name; auto-filled from city if left empty; empty + timed birth = LMT mode)
index.f_houses_placidus: Placidus (default; most common in modern Western practice)
index.houses_note: Koch and other quadrant systems are not computed in this browser build (see methodology); the Python lab kernel supports more systems.
index.f_question: Question (optional; the static text does not answer outcome questions)
index.consent: I consent to anonymous usage measurement of this research prototype (no birth data; never linked to my answers; never fed to interpretation).
index.unknown_time: I don't know my birth time
index.education: The Ascendant, MC and house cusps shift roughly every 4 minutes of birth time, so they cannot be determined without it. Planets' positions within signs barely move during a day. If you don't know the time, don't invent one: the tool will honestly hide what cannot be computed without it (Moon degree, angles, houses) and show what can (planets in signs, planetary aspects).
index.engine_note: Engine: {engine} {version} — the verified Python kernel's browser port · tropical zodiac · planetary positions from astronomy-engine 2.1.19 · differentially verified against the Python kernel (260 frozen cases, 0 failures) · time zone history from the IANA tzdb · house cusps per selected system (school-labeled).

about.title: SFERA Lab — Methodology & Provenance
about.description: Calculation method, conventions, two-layer verification record, school labels and honest limitations of the SFERA Lab natal chart generator.
about.what: SFERA Lab is a research instrument, not a commercial product. This page computes real Western tropical natal charts and displays them with their conventions labeled. It generates no AI text. It exists because the SFERA research program needs a verified deterministic calculation layer, and because a free, honest chart tool is genuinely useful. This is a Research UI, deliberately not a finished product interface.
method_rows: astronomy-engine 2.1.19 (MIT, analytic ephemeris — the same library version as the verified Python kernel), geocentric ecliptic-of-date longitudes; retrograde states from numeric 1-hour central-difference speeds.

IANA tzdb via the browser/Node Intl database — the authoritative source for historical offsets, DST and LMT-era births. Nonexistent local times (DST spring gaps) are rejected, not silently shifted. Ambiguous fall-back times are labeled and resolved explicitly (fold 0/1). The zone identity (e.g. Asia/Yekaterinburg) comes from the place-resolution result, never inferred from a current UTC offset.

Native formulas for ASC/MC and Placidus, equal and whole-sign systems, computed in your browser. House systems genuinely disagree away from the angles — that is a documented feature of the tradition; the system used is always labeled. Koch, Regiomontanus and Campanus are computed by the Python lab kernel but are not implemented in this browser build (honestly absent, never approximated).
Mean node via the analytic secular formula. The true (osculating) node requires the lab kernel's library and is suppressed here.
Major aspects (0/60/90/120/180) with one documented natal orb set (config orbs-v0.1); the convention is disclosed rather than hidden.
Unknown birth time → Moon degree, angles and houses are suppressed, never approximated. Beyond ±66° latitude angles and houses are suppressed (school-dependent to the point of being undefined).
about.verif_h: Verification (two layers, both frozen and committed)
about.verif_py: Python kernel {py} vs Swiss Ephemeris (pyswisseph) + published oracle anchors (equinoxes/solstices/new moons)
about.verif_py_note: — 51 frozen verification cases, max cross-engine delta {delta}°. Engine-vs-engine agreement is NOT proof of truth, and is labeled as such.
about.verif_js: This browser port ({engine} {version}) vs the Python kernel
about.verif_js_note: — 260 frozen cases (positions, 16 historical time-zone batteries, 192 house-system cases across 8 latitudes, mean node, full-chart pipelines, byte-level reading-template comparison): {failures} failures. Layer maxima: positions {pos}° (same library lineage — not an independent cross-check; the independent cross-engine check is the Python kernel's {pydelta}° vs Swiss Ephemeris) · time zones {tz} s · houses {houses}° · mean node {node}°. The committed record and fixture are in the public repository.
about.schools: Western tropical astrology is not one thing. Where a convention matters (house system, orb set, node type), this tool shows which one was used. The only interpretive surface is the labeled static template, which lists calculated positions and deliberately suppresses what is unknown — it makes no claims beyond the chart's geometry.
about.status: The lab has run an internal quality benchmark of AI interpretation (X-01-Z) and maintains an evidence database and claim ledger — see the live research status page, generated from the repository. What is not validated: human practitioner acceptance, the engine bet on voluntary return, willingness to pay. No research claims are made beyond what exists.
about.privacy: The calculation runs in your browser; birth data never leaves your device; there is no server to receive it. Full explanation: privacy page — including an honest description of what the place search sends.
about.city: Place search uses a hybrid: a small bundled city list (coordinates ≈±1 km, verification class UNVERIFIED_COMPILED_LIST) plus the global Open-Meteo/GeoNames gazetteer (CC-BY 4.0; the query is sent only when you search; gazetteer precision is roughly a kilometer, less for small localities). The time zone is taken as an IANA identity and applied with the full historical tzdb. For archival precision, enter latitude/longitude and the time zone manually. Suggestion ranking: exact matches outrank prefix matches, which outrank one-letter variants («Кагул» ↔ «Кахул»); a large city (≥100k) is promoted above an unpopulated same-spelling hamlet — all options remain listed, only the order changes. Place-resolution regression cases (incl. Tyumen and Cahul) are frozen in the lab repository.

labstatus.title: SFERA Lab — Live Research Status
labstatus.description: Real-time counts derived from the SFERA Lab repository: evidence records, claim ledger, benchmark corpus, experiment states, scientific-source integrity.
labstatus.intro: Every number on this page is derived at build time from the repository's real objects (evidence DB, claim ledger, corpus, run ledger, source-status registry, experiment files). If the repository changes, a rebuild changes this page. There are no vanity counters — a counter that cannot be derived is not shown.
labstatus.bykind_note: "SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE" is the evidence-database class, not a claim that astrology is scientifically supported: the class includes null results (e.g. Carlson 1985; Dean & Kelly 2003), retracted sources (Brooks 2016 — recorded as retracted, excluded from active support), and psychology studies unrelated to astrology's validity. Composition: see the evidence DB.
labstatus.claims_note: Claims marked prohibited_for_public_use ({n}) are permanently banned from public copy; the build-time claim audit fails the release if their phrasing appears anywhere on this site.
labstatus.retracted_th: source ({status}) — recorded, excluded from active support, not deleted
labstatus.sources_rule_note: Only 'active' (or corrected) sources count as usable scientific support; retracted sources are recorded, never cited as support, never deleted.
labstatus.telemetry_note: Later funnel stages (offer/checkout/paid) do not exist; none may be simulated. This page reports them as NOT_IMPLEMENTED rather than as zero-conversion steps of a paywall that isn't there.
labstatus.publicval_notmeasured: Not measured: the central telemetry sink is not connected. 'Not measured' is never rendered as zero.

labstatus.publicval_note: The numbers above are consented, HUMAN_LIKELY traffic only — no internal QA, no bots. Internal QA traffic is explicitly marked and excluded from organic validation.
